name: Terminate a manager and transition its assets
function: external manager research and total portfolio management
summary: When an external mandate is terminated or resized, or a new client's legacy managers are replaced, the manager research team and a total portfolio manager plan how to move the assets: in kind to a new manager or internal team, sold by the legacy manager, or traded by a transition manager chosen on its cost estimate. Legal reads the termination clause, the director signs the notice, operations switches trading authority at the custodian and compliance suspends the old rules. Trading itself takes days, but closing the old account waits weeks to months for final fees, trailing income and tax reclaims, and poorly timed notices or delays add unmeasured market and cost risk.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial public-sector asset manager of about 240 staff that cut its roster from 200 to 124 managers in 2020 and kept replacing legacy mandates afterwards.
baseline.notes: The termination decision is made in manager monitoring; final fee payment runs in the manager fee process; cash raised or freed is redeployed in pool rebalancing.

trigger: The chief investment officer approves a termination or resize decision, or a new client's legacy transition plan names a manager to replace.
end_state: The assets sit with the target mandates, the transition cost has been reviewed and the legacy account is closed after final fees and residual cash are settled.

volume.seasonality: About six a month in 2020 during the roster cut, then one or two a month.

evidence.note: Roster cut from 200 to 124 in 2020 (76 fewer managers, including underlying funds) and planned at 80 to 85 by mid-2021; the 2021-2022 mode is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Open the transition file
steps.description: The manager research analyst receives the approved termination or resize decision, or a new client's legacy manager plan, pulls the management agreement's termination clause, the latest holdings and the target mandates, and sets up the transition checklist and team.
inputs: termination decision or legacy transition plan

evidence.note: Identify administrative issues such as notification periods and termination clauses.

steps.name: Review the termination terms and draft the notice
steps.description: Investment counsel reads the agreement's termination clause (notice period, effective date, fees on termination, return of records, duty to cooperate with a successor or transition manager) and drafts the termination notice and instructions to stop trading.

evidence.note: Agreements set termination procedures for either party.

steps.name: Choose the transition method and target allocation
steps.description: The total portfolio manager compares legacy holdings with the target mandates or internal portfolios, estimates overlap for in-kind transfer, decides between in-kind transfer, liquidation by the legacy manager or a transition manager, and plans interim market exposure and currency hedging.

error.defect_description: Overlap or liquidity of legacy holdings is misjudged, so trading takes longer or costs more.

next.condition: large or multi-asset move: use a transition manager
in-kind transfer, internal team or legacy manager liquidation

evidence.note: Cost comparison of in-specie transfer versus liquidation; FX hedging; target managers are not always best placed. Split is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Request pre-trade estimates from transition managers
steps.description: The analyst sends the legacy and target portfolios, under confidentiality, to two or three transition managers on the organisation's panel and asks for a pre-trade cost estimate, strategy and conflicts disclosure on a standard template.

evidence.note: T-Charter pro forma cost estimate templates; selection on estimates and conflicts.

steps.name: Wait for the pre-trade estimates
steps.description: The transition managers analyse the liquidity of each holding and the overlap with the target portfolio and return an estimated implementation shortfall by cost component, a trading strategy and a timetable.

evidence.note: Two to seven days, author's estimate.

steps.name: Compare estimates and choose the transition manager
steps.description: The analyst compares the estimates like for like, checks crossing and conflicts disclosures and the proposed strategy, and recommends a transition manager in the transition plan.

evidence.note: Judge on capability, solution and conflicts, not only cheapest price.

steps.name: Approve the transition plan
steps.description: The director of manager research reviews the method, cost estimate, timetable, interim exposure and any transition manager appointment, and approves the plan or sends it back.

control.basis: Delegation of authority for transition plans and transition manager appointments

evidence.note: Estimate the costs of changing managers and develop strategies to minimise them.

steps.name: Sign and send the termination notice
steps.description: The director signs the notice and instructions, timed with the transition manager or target manager so information does not leak, and sends it to the legacy manager with any transition manager appointment letter.

control.basis: Signing authority for termination notices under the management agreement

evidence.note: Common practice; information leakage concern from transition literature.

steps.name: Wait for the legacy manager to acknowledge and stop trading
steps.description: The legacy manager acknowledges the notice, stops discretionary trading from the effective time and sends its final holdings and open trade report.

evidence.note: One to seven days, author's estimate.

steps.name: Instruct the custodian and switch trading authority
steps.description: The trade settlement analyst sends the custodian authorised instructions to remove the legacy manager's trading authority, add the transition or target manager, set up any transition account and update settlement instructions, confirming by call-back.

error.defect_description: Legacy authority not removed in time or wrong instructions, so a trade settles in the wrong account.

control.basis: Authorised signatory instructions to the custodian with call-back verification

evidence.note: Account modification documentation must be received, authenticated and set up accurately.

steps.name: Suspend the legacy compliance rules and set transition limits
steps.description: The compliance analyst switches the legacy mandate's rules to transition status so expected deviations do not raise breaches, and sets the limits that apply to the transition account.

control.basis: OSC exemption order: policies to prevent investments that contravene IMA restrictions

evidence.note: Restrictions must be enforced by controls; transition treatment is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Lock the trade list and transition day
steps.description: The total portfolio manager confirms final legacy holdings, the target portfolios from the receiving managers, the in-kind lists, currency hedges and any futures overlay, and gives the go to trade.

evidence.note: Legacy asset list received five days before trading started.

steps.name: Transition trading and in-kind transfers
steps.description: The transition manager or receiving manager trades the legacy holdings into the target portfolio, the custodian moves in-kind securities between accounts and currency trades are executed.

evidence.note: Trading for a nine-mandate transition completed within six days.

steps.name: Monitor settlement of transition trades and transfers
steps.description: The trade settlement analyst tracks settlement of the transition trades, in-kind deliveries and currency trades, chases fails with the custodian and brokers and confirms the legacy account holds only residual cash.

evidence.note: Common practice; fail share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Confirm target exposures and release residual cash
steps.description: The total portfolio manager checks the receiving mandates and internal portfolios hold the intended allocation, removes any interim overlay and sends residual cash to pool rebalancing.

evidence.note: Common practice.

steps.name: Review the post-transition report
steps.description: The analyst reviews the transition manager's or receiving manager's post-trade report, compares implementation shortfall by component with the estimate, questions unexplained costs or delays and files the result.

evidence.note: Implementation shortfall against the estimate is the standard measure; post-transition report compares actual and estimate.

steps.name: Wait for final fees, income and trailing items
steps.description: The legacy manager's final fee invoice is validated and paid in the fee process, and dividends, coupons, tax reclaims and corporate action proceeds still arrive in the legacy account.

evidence.note: Final fee invoices usually follow the quarter end; trailing income takes weeks to months.

steps.name: Sweep residual cash and request account closure
steps.description: The trade settlement analyst sweeps residual cash and trailing income to the pool account, confirms no open items, reclaims or securities remain, and sends the custodian an authorised closure instruction.

control.basis: Authorised signatory instructions to the custodian

next.condition: a reclaim or income item still outstanding

evidence.note: Common practice.

steps.name: Wait for the custodian to close the account
steps.description: The custodian checks that no positions, cash or pending items remain, closes the account and its market sub-accounts with its agent banks and sends a written closure confirmation.

evidence.note: One to three weeks, author's estimate.

steps.name: Close the file and update records
steps.description: The analyst marks the mandate terminated in the manager research database, asks data management and compliance to retire feeds and rules, stores the transition records and reports the cost to the director.

evidence.note: Common practice.

exceptions.name: Transition manager appointed
exceptions.description: Large or multi-asset moves use a transition manager selected on pre-trade estimates.

exceptions.name: Plan sent back
exceptions.description: The director asks for a different method or timing, for example to keep market exposure during the move.

exceptions.name: Settlement fails during the transition
exceptions.description: In-kind deliveries or trades fail and are chased, delaying the release of residual cash.

exceptions.name: Trailing items keep the account open
exceptions.description: A tax reclaim, class action or late income keeps the legacy account open for further months.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from termination decision to legacy account closed
benchmarks.population: Segregated external mandates terminated by an institutional investor

evidence.note: Author's estimate; 70% of US transitions in 2015 had a delay or implementation period of 1 to 12 months, and account closure adds the wait for final fees and trailing income.
Trading completed within the first six days.
From 200 to 124, including underlying funds.

pain_points.description: Time between the decision and the move is rarely measured; delays in plans, approvals and notices leave assets with a manager the organisation no longer wants.

evidence.note: Event shortfall and delays of one to twelve months.

pain_points.description: Transition cost is judged on estimates and post-trade reports from the parties doing the work, so in-house review is needed to spot unexplained costs.
Closing the legacy account drags on for months because of final fee invoices, trailing income and tax reclaims.

evidence.note: General practice.

pain_points.description: Many parties (legacy and receiving managers, transition manager, custodian, internal teams) coordinate by email around a fixed transition day.

evidence.note: 17 parties and over 1,000 emails in one transition.

sources.title: Selecting, Reviewing and Replacing Managers
sources.publisher: Western University pension plans (Joint Pension Board)
sources.supports: On a terminate recommendation: withhold future cash flows, terminate and invoke a pre-agreed backup manager, search for a replacement, identify and estimate the costs of changing managers with strategies to minimise them, and identify administrative issues such as notification periods and termination clauses; administrative problems include failure to report and incomplete documentation.

sources.title: Top Ten Tips For Transition Management (MJ Hudson)
sources.supports: Delays from infrequent meetings, searches, legal negotiation and operations; implementation shortfall is the industry standard cost measure; transition managers chosen on cost estimates should also be judged on solution and conflicts; target managers are not always best placed to transition legacy assets; hedge FX during transitions; citing State Street research, 70% of US transitions in 2015 had a delay or implementation period of 1 to 12 months.

sources.title: Client case study: Managing transition costs when consolidating pension funds
sources.supports: Nine legacy mandates, 17 parties, over 1,000 emails and weekly project calls; pre-transition cost comparison of in-specie transfer versus liquidation; legacy asset list received 14 February, trading started 19 February and completed within six days in line with the pre-trade estimate; post-transition report compared actual implementation shortfall with the estimate.

sources.title: Confessions of a transition manager
sources.supports: T-Standard (2003) is the industry method for implementation shortfall measured from the last close before the transition manager has all information to trade; T-Charter (2007) sets ten principles and pro forma cost estimate templates; implementation shortfall components include commissions, taxes, spreads, market impact and opportunity cost; without measurement there is no accountability.

sources.title: The model manager 2020 Annual Report
sources.supports: 200 fund managers (including underlying funds) in mid-2019, 124 at end 2020 and a plan for about 80 to 85 by mid-2021; fund-of-funds eliminated; one-time manager transition costs in 2020 from repositioning public equity portfolios; hedge fund portfolio moved from fund-of-funds to direct hedge fund investments on a managed account platform; senior roles filled to support more direct and co-investing; a client engagement protocol rolled out to all employees in December 2020 setting guidelines and accountability for client communications.

sources.title: The model manager posts solid 2020 return, meets benchmark index (news release)
sources.publisher: The model manager via Cision Newswire
sources.supports: External manager roster cut from 200 to 124 in 2020, fund-of-funds eliminated, new strategic partnerships formed and about $10 million of investment management fees saved.

sources.title: Selecting Third-Party Investment Professionals for Pension Fund Assets (best practice)
sources.supports: Management agreement should name account personnel and fiduciary duties, commit to the investment policy, require prompt notice of ownership or key personnel changes, set reporting, insurance, fee, invoicing and payment terms and termination procedures for either party; review a transition and implementation plan; ongoing risk control with at least annual compliance review, guideline compliance checks and timely reconciliations.

sources.title: The model manager, Commission and Director decisions (exemption order, June 2017)
sources.supports: Board-approved policies required for: a compliance system and a chief compliance officer; books and records; conflicts including insider trading and front running; prevention of any investment that contravenes the investment restrictions set out in each member's IMA; a KYC policy; an escalation process for member concerns or complaints that may be set out in the IMA; a due diligence process for vetting and monitoring sub-advisers; due diligence on custodians and brokers before they hold or access assets.

sources.title: Asset Manager's Guide to SOC 1 (June 2017)
sources.supports: Baseline control objectives: documentation for opening and modifying accounts is received, authenticated and set up accurately and timely; trades follow portfolio guidelines and account restrictions (client investment guideline and restriction compliance); positions and cash reconcile to custodian records with breaks researched and resolved; client account statements are complete, correct and timely; fee calculation and billing listed as an area to consider.

assumptions: The transition manager is drawn from a pre-approved panel, so no separate procurement is modelled; its trading and the custodian's transfers are modelled as an external wait.
Final fee validation and payment run in the manager fee process; this workflow only waits for them before closing the account.
About 40% of cases use a transition manager; the rest move in kind to a receiving manager or internal team or are sold by the legacy manager.
Hedge fund redemptions on the managed account platform follow the hedge fund dealing process and are not counted here, although they formed part of the 2020 roster cut.
Roles, titles and hourly costs come from the organisation file; full-time equivalents are set from simulated hands-on time times volume, using the 1.5 a month mode rather than the 2020 peak.
